title: 第二十二章 露怯
content_zh:
第二天是逢五的集。

    云中城坊市逢五逢十有大集，四乡八里的人都往城里挤，卖菜的、卖柴的、卖针头线脑的，把本就不宽的街塞得水泄不通。江砚的小铺子这天生意也好，一上午写了七八封信，手都没歇过。

    晌午过后，集上忽然起了一阵骚动。

    江砚听见前头人声乱，有人喊，有人骂，还有女人尖着嗓子哭。他探出头看，只见斜对面卖布的摊子前，围了一圈人。

    围着的中心，是个穿绸子的胖汉，带着两个膀大腰圆的家丁，正揪着一个卖布的老头的衣领，把那老头按在自家摊子上。

    “你这老东西,睁眼说瞎话!”胖汉唾沫横飞，“爷昨儿在你这儿买的布,回去一量,短了三尺!你还敢讹爷的钱?”

    那卖布老头脸涨得通红，挣着辩：“客官，没有的事啊!我这布,尺尺都是足的,街坊都能作证——”

    “放屁!”胖汉一巴掌扇过去，老头一个趔趄,栽在地上。旁边一个十来岁的小姑娘——许是老头的孙女——扑过去护着爷爷,哇地哭了出来。

    围观的人不少，可没一个敢上前。

    江砚认得那胖汉。这人是城里一个布商的远房亲戚，仗着有点钱有点势,在坊市里横惯了，谁见了都绕道走。今儿这事，明摆着是讹诈——昨日他根本没在这老头摊上买过布，分明是看人老实可欺，编个由头来敲一笔。

    “爷今儿不要你赔钱了。”胖汉冷笑，一脚踢翻老头的布摊,整匹整匹的粗布滚了一地,沾了泥水，“爷要你这摊子!这布,这架子,全充了爷的赔款!来人,搬!”

    两个家丁应声上去搬布。

    那小姑娘死死抱着一匹布不撒手，被一个家丁拎小鸡似的拎起来,往地上一甩。小姑娘的头磕在石阶角上,登时见了血。

    老头疯了一样扑过去:“囡囡!囡囡!”

    人群里有人倒吸冷气，却还是没人动。

    江砚的拳头，在袖子里慢慢攥紧了。

    他认得这种事。这种把人按在地上、夺人活路、还要人闭嘴的事。他在沈家村受过，骨头里记着。那种被踩着、被抢着、连一块饼都护不住的滋味,他这辈子都忘不了。

    他知道自己不该出头。

    他来路不明，身上还背着“逃奴”的罪名，最该做的是缩着头，当没看见。秦伯说过,乱世里头，能活着就别嫌路脏。

    可那小姑娘头上的血，和老头那声“囡囡”，像两根针,直直地扎进他心里。

    他终究没忍住。

    江砚搁下笔，从铺子里走了出去。

    “住手。”

    声音不大，可坊市里头乱糟糟的，他这一开口，竟让近处几个人都回了头。

    胖汉斜眼瞅他，见是个面生的瘦少年,嗤笑一声：“哪来的雏儿,管闲事?”

    “你昨儿没在他摊上买过布。”江砚走近几步，目光扫过那地上滚落的布匹，又落回胖汉脸上，“他这布是松江来的细棉,你说的‘短了三尺’——你倒说说，你买的是哪一匹,什么花色,什么纹路?”

    胖汉一噎。
content_en:
The next day is the Friday episode.

    There is a big market every fifth and tenth day in Yunzhong Chengfang City, and people from all over the country crowd into the city. Vegetable sellers, firewood sellers, and needlework and thread sellers crowd the narrow streets. Jiang Yan's small shop was doing a good job that day. He wrote seven or eight letters all morning without resting his hands.

    After noon, there was a sudden commotion on the market.

    Jiang Yan heard the chaos in front of him, some shouting, some scolding, and a woman crying with a sharp voice. He stuck his head out and saw a circle of people gathered in front of the cloth stall diagonally opposite.

    In the center of the crowd was a fat man in silk, accompanied by two servants with big shoulders and round waists. They were grabbing an old man selling cloth by his collar and pressing him against his stall.

    "You old man, you are telling lies!" the fat man spat, "The cloth I bought from you yesterday was measured when I went back and it was three feet short! How dare you extort my money?"

    The old cloth seller's face turned red and he tried to argue: "Sir, it's nothing! I have enough cloth, and every neighbor can testify that-"

    "Fart!" The fat man slapped him, and the old man staggered and fell to the ground. A teenage girl next to him - Xu was the old man's granddaughter - rushed over to protect her grandfather and burst into tears.

    There were many people watching, but no one dared to come forward.

    Jiang Yan recognized the fat man. This man was a distant relative of a cloth merchant in the city. He had a little money and a lot of influence. He was so used to being a bully in the market that everyone he saw would avoid him. What happened today was obviously blackmail - he didn't buy any cloth from this old man's stall yesterday. He was obviously looking at people who were honest and could be deceived, so he made up a pretext to make a fortune.

    "I don't want you to pay compensation today." The fat man sneered and kicked over the old man's cloth stall. The whole piece of coarse cloth rolled on the floor and was stained with muddy water. "I want your stall! This cloth and this shelf are all filled with my compensation! Come on, move it!"

    The two servants responded and went up to move the cloth.

    The little girl hugged a piece of cloth tightly and refused to let go. A servant picked her up like a chicken and threw her to the ground. The little girl's head hit the corner of the stone steps and blood immediately appeared.

    The old man rushed over like crazy: "Nanny! Nanny!"

    Some people in the crowd gasped, but no one moved.

    Jiang Yan's fists slowly clenched in his sleeves.

    He recognized this kind of thing. This kind of thing involves pinning people to the ground, taking away their means of survival, and forcing them to shut up. He had experienced it in Shenjia Village, and it was remembered in his bones. He would never forget the feeling of being stepped on, being robbed, and not being able to protect even a piece of cake.

    He knew he shouldn't come forward.

    His origin is unknown, and he is still accused of being a "fugitive slave." The best thing to do is to shrink your head and pretend you don't see him. Uncle Qin once said that in troubled times, if you can survive, don't worry about the dirty roads.

    But the blood on the little girl's head and the old man's "Nanny" were like two needles, piercing straight into his heart.

    He couldn't hold it back after all.

    Jiang Yan put down his pen and walked out of the shop.

    "Stop."

    His voice was not loud, but the city was in chaos. His words made several people nearby turn their heads.

    The fat man squinted at him and saw that he was an unfamiliar, skinny boy. He sneered, "Where do you think you are, meddling in other people's business?"

    "You didn't buy any cloth from his stall yesterday." Jiang Yan took a few steps closer and glanced at the cloth rolling on the ground, then returned to the fat man's face. "The cloth he made is fine cotton from Songjiang. You said it was 'three feet short' - tell me which piece you bought, what color, and what texture?"

    The fat man choked.
